doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

title: First paid gigs at 13 and Jaski's double-booking
summary: He started playing gigs very young, earned $20 the first time, and played with older musicians. Jaski would send him out with an amp and then show up partway through the night.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Did you decide, yourself, at some point, that your career or your livelihood was going to be in music or did it just sort of happen?
It just happened. I started playing very young, gigs. By the time I was 13 I was out on the weekends making money and, you know, and that was it. Once I got money in my pocket I was good to go.
Can you remember the first time you made money and how much was it?

That was a lot. Yeah. I was knocked out by that. They didn’t all pay that, and some of those things I did early on they passed the hats, they were little things at the Moose Club and those kinds of things. Always with the older musicians, I was always the kid. And John Jaski at the time, my accordion teacher, he had a band and he would double book himself, and then he would send me out on a gig, with his amp, you know he’d give me an amp and I’d bring the accordion and I’d play with a couple of guys somewhere. sometime during the night he would leave one place and he’d just go show up at the other place, just like “hi folks, here I am.”
You know we both need someone like that, to do that.
Yeah. You go there and play the first half hour.
We should do that. Yeah. Absolutely.
